reports.title: Notification of Government Deficit and Debt
reports.description: ČSÚ's biannual EDP notification release for general government deficit and debt, submitted to Eurostat each March and September and compiled per ESA 2010. The release does not itself name Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 or use the acronym "EDP" — checked directly against the raw page text, not inferred.

reports.title: Government Deficit and Debt According to EMU Definitions
reports.description: CBS's official landing page for the Netherlands' EDP notification under Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 — states the notification procedure's legal basis and the excessive-deficit threshold, and hosts the actual notification tables supplied to Eurostat. The ESA 2010 compilation statement lives on CBS's companion definitions page for the same underlying figures, not on this page itself.

reports.title: Government Deficit and Debt (Notification to the European Commission)
reports.publisher: INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques)
reports.description: INSEE's twice-yearly (end of March / end of September) national-accounts release on general government deficit and debt, explicitly stated as the assessment used to notify France's public debt and deficit to the European Commission. Checked both this release and INSEE's companion Maastricht-debt release for an ESA 2010/SEC 2010 or Regulation 479/2009 citation — neither document names either.

reports.title: Government Deficit and Debt in the EU Countries (Denmark)
reports.description: Danmarks Statistik's biannual EDP notification release (ØMU-saldo/ØMU-gæld). Compiled per ESA 2010 and under Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 — both cited in the statistic's own official documentation page rather than the press release body — and explicitly produced for the two semi-annual EDP notifications to Eurostat.

reports.title: Notification of General Government Deficit and Debt According to the Excessive Deficit Procedure
reports.description: ISTAT's biannual EDP notification release, explicitly self-described as Italy's notification to the European Commission within the Excessive Deficit Procedure and compiled per the ESA 2010 system of national accounts. Does not itself name Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 by number — checked directly, not inferred.

_dropped.why: MODELLING DECISION, not a research gap. uk-edp-inventory is a pre-Brexit (December 2015, per its own filename) ONS Article 9 inventory; its original PDF is now dead (link rot). The European Commission's own EDP page for the UK states outright: "The United Kingdom was a member of the European Union from 1973 until 31 January 2020. The information contained on this page relates to its time as a member." ONS's own Public Sector Finances QMI confirms the reporting channel itself stopped: "The rules governing the new relationship between the EU and UK took effect on 1 January 2021, after which the UK stopped supplying Eurostat with EDP data" — and frames the whole topic under a section literally titled "UK's compliance with the Maastricht Treaty while a member of the EU." ONS's EDP-branded release series last published 19 October 2020 with no successor announced since. There is no live UK release produced under a current EDP obligation to wire — the obligation itself ended, this isn't an access or evidence-quality problem. Per rule 2, don't force an edge to a document (Public Sector Finances QMI) that only discusses this in the past tense and redirects successor reporting to the IMF/OECD, not the EU. uk-edp-inventory stays wired only to eu-reg-479-2009 and esa-2010, as before — this is a closed, deliberate non-mint, not an open lead.

Genuine research gap, not blocked access. The one plausible candidate found — STATEC's Note de Conjoncture N°1-2026 (biannual economic-outlook bulletin, Chapter 5 'Finances publiques', published ~24 March 2026, just ahead of the April 1 EDP deadline) — reports Luxembourg's deficit/GDP figure but does not itself state that these ARE the notified EDP figures, does not name ESA 2010/SEC 2010, and does not name Council Regulation 479/2009 or the EDP — checked against the full text of both this edition and the prior (September 2025) edition. STATEC's only other mention of Regulation 479/2009 site-wide is a bare link-list entry on a general, undated methodology page (comptes-administrations-publiques.html), not a sentence — fails the same bar LU's inventory node itself would need to clear. STATEC's SDDS-Plus government-finance dissemination (GGO/GGD categories) is raw Excel/XML with no narrative text at all. Checked STATEC's actualites/publications RSS feeds (~1 year back): no dedicated deficit/debt press release exists as a standalone item. LEAD for a future round: STATEC may publish a formal Article 9-referenced notification only as a non-indexed PDF (the pattern several other countries' EDP releases follow) — worth a targeted site search or a direct request to STATEC's press office rather than another general web search. RESOLVED 2026-08-30: found via Eurostat's own EDP notification-tables index -- Luxembourg's April 2026 Article 9 notification (LU-2026-04.pdf), hosted on ec.europa.eu's central document repository, explicitly names Regulation 479/2009 and ESA 2010 in its own header. New node lu-govfin minted -- see eu-unlinked-wiring-round-2026-08-30.json.
